goal: Connect the picker failure to the Windows App SDK preview self-contained single-project packaging resource issue and give a safe fix or workaround.
must_include: Uses the fixture details to identify the failing combination as Windows App SDK 1.8 preview, packaged MSIX, `WindowsAppSDKSelfContained=true`, and the new `Microsoft.Windows.Storage.Pickers.FolderPicker`.
Mentions the upstream issue was missing packaged PRI/resource files and was fixed in Windows App SDK 1.8 / newer MSIX build tooling.
Recommends upgrading to a fixed Windows App SDK or directly referencing `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.MSIX` 1.7.20250829.1 or later when staying on the affected preview.
Gives a workaround such as using a separate packaging project or running unpackaged while waiting for the fixed tooling.
must_not: Blames the `AppWindow.Id` constructor call as the primary bug in this fixture.
Suggests adding broad file-system capabilities as the fix for the picker creation exception.
Tells the developer to run elevated to make the picker work.
acceptable_alternatives: Move from the preview SDK to the latest stable Windows App SDK that contains the packaging fix.
Use an external Windows Application Packaging Project until the single-project packaging toolchain is updated.
Temporarily disable self-contained packaging if that matches the app's deployment needs.
solved: The answer tells the developer to update or work around the affected self-contained single-project packaging toolchain rather than rewriting the picker code.
partial: The answer notices the issue is tied to self-contained packaging but does not name an upgrade or packaging workaround.
notes: The log intentionally contains only the runtime exception and debug noise; the missing PRI cause is in the source issue comments, not in the fixture log.
